Data Cleaning¶

Make Dummies¶

In [66]:
df["Sex"] = df["Sex"].map({"F": 0, "M": 1})
df["ExerciseAngina"] = df["ExerciseAngina"].map({"N": 0, "Y": 1})
df = pd.get_dummies(
    df,
    columns=["ChestPainType", "RestingECG", "ST_Slope"],
    drop_first=False,
    prefix=["ChestPainType", "RestingECG", "ST_Slope"]
)

bool_cols = df.select_dtypes(include='bool').columns
df[bool_cols] = df[bool_cols].astype(int)
df = df.drop(columns=["ChestPainType_ASY", "RestingECG_Normal", "ST_Slope_Flat"]) # I dropped these variables to avoid multicollinearity and chose to remove the baseline for consistency

Outliers¶

In [67]:
def remove_outliers_iqr(df, columns):
    df_clean = df.copy()
    
    for col in columns:
        Q1 = df_clean[col].quantile(0.25)
        Q3 = df_clean[col].quantile(0.75)
        IQR = Q3 - Q1
        lower = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
        upper = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
        
        df_clean = df_clean[(df_clean[col] >= lower) & (df_clean[col] <= upper)]
    
    return df_clean

outlier_cols = ["RestingBP", "Cholesterol", "Oldpeak", "Age",  "MaxHR"]
df = remove_outliers_iqr(df, outlier_cols)

Feature Engineering¶

In [72]:
df_feature_engineering = df.copy()
df_feature_engineering["log_oldpeak"] = np.log(1 + df_feature_engineering["Oldpeak"]) # Since old peak is right skewed we loged transformed it
df_feature_engineering.drop(columns=["Oldpeak"], inplace=True)

# We know of the trend that men develop heart disease at younger ages compared to woman so we wanted to see if sex changes the effect of other variables
df_feature_engineering["Age_Sex_inter"] = df_feature_engineering["Age"] * df_feature_engineering["Sex"]
df_feature_engineering["RestingBP_Sex_inter"] = df_feature_engineering["RestingBP"] * df_feature_engineering["Sex"]
df_feature_engineering["Cholesterol_Sex_inter"] = df_feature_engineering["Cholesterol"] * df_feature_engineering["Sex"]
df_feature_engineering["MaxHR_Sex_inter"] = df_feature_engineering["MaxHR"] * df_feature_engineering["Sex"]

# Read that fasting blood sugar and cholestorol might increase impact of each other on heart disease risk
df_feature_engineering["Cholesterol_FastingBS_inter"] = df_feature_engineering["Cholesterol"] * df_feature_engineering["FastingBS"]
df_feature_engineering

Observations:

For regularization, LASSO shrinks nothing to exactly 0. Ridge and Elastic Net shrink some variables very significantly: Sex, RestingBP_Sex_inter, Cholesterol_Sex_inter, MaxHR_Sex_inter, Cholesterol_FastingBS_inter, and ST_Slope_Up.

All heavily-shrunk variables except Sex and ST_Slope_Up were statistically insignificant in the unregularized model because their p-values > 0.05 so this is strong evidence that these variables likely add little predictive power to our model.

Test reduced model against full model with likelihood ratio test¶

In [45]:
LL_full = full_model.llf
LL_reduced = reduced_model.llf

LR_stat = -2 * (LL_reduced - LL_full)
degree_freedom = full_model.df_model - reduced_model.df_model
pval = chi2.sf(LR_stat, degree_freedom)

print("Likelihood Ratio Test")
print("LR statistic:", LR_stat)
print("Degrees of freedom:", degree_freedom)
print("p-value:", pval)

Likelihood Ratio Test
LR statistic: 17.371826939473124
Degrees of freedom: 14.0
p-value: 0.23690409734101112

Null Hypothesis is that the reduced model fits the data just as well as the full model. Since p-val is above 0.05, fails to reject this. The simpler model is sufficient.

X_red_for_vif = pd.DataFrame(X_red_train, columns=X_red_train.columns)
